prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web app decision comp, 1440x1000 landscape
Primary request: Design the Neuronauts VS-mode live match as an “Airlock Arena”: two opposing team bays visibly face each other and open around one shared semantic field. This is an operational game screen, not a poster.
Input images: Image 1 is a visual identity reference only. Carry over its near-black green canvas, matte outlined panels, Avenir-like workhorse sans typography, crisp custom pixel-glyph character, compact astronaut avatars, restrained spacing, and no-glow/no-glass/no-gradient discipline. Do not copy the landing-page content or layout.
Structure: persistent slim mission header; left third Red Shift team bay with red signal rail, 3 player avatars/names/typing states and per-person stats; center third semantic space with many tiny red and blue points around an unlabeled target, large readable team score confrontation and match phase; right third Blue Orbit team bay with blue signal rail and equivalent telemetry; below, the current player’s guess console and private flight log are clearly readable while opponent words never appear. Show guess count, average %, best %, hints, and overall progress for both teams. One team may show FINISHED while the other shows STILL SEARCHING.
Style/medium: polished production web UI screenshot, flat matte controls and surfaces, purposeful asymmetry within an overall face-off composition, authentic semantic word-game data.
Color palette: #101613 canvas, #171f1c panels, off-white text, restrained teal utility accent, #d95a5a red team, #5b91d8 blue team, amber only for hints.
Text (verbatim where prominent): “RED SHIFT”, “BLUE ORBIT”, “VS”, “SEMANTIC SPACE”, “YOUR FLIGHT LOG”, “Transmit guess”, “Still searching”.
Constraints: opponent points are visible but opponent word labels are absent; own words may be visible; clear 44px controls; no invented commercial claims; no gradients, glassmorphism, neon glow, generic lucide icons, bento-card collage, or excessive rounded capsules. Make the first viewport feel unmistakably competitive and immediately usable.
